units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
So much marriage is certainly not becoming. Twenty years of romance make a woman look like a ruin; but twenty years of marriage make her something like a public building.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Twenty years of romance! Is there such a thing?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Not in our day. Women have become too brilliant. Nothing spoils a romance so much as a sense of humour in the woman.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Or the want of it in the man.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: You are quite right. In a Temple every one should be serious, except the thing that is worshipped.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: And that should be man?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Women kneel so gracefully; men don’t.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You are thinking of Lady Stutfield!
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I assure you I have not thought of Lady Stutfield for the last quarter of an hour.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Is she such a mystery?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: She is more than a mystery—she is a mood.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Moods don’t last.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: It is their chief charm.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Enter HESTER and GERALD.
Lord Illingworth, every one has been congratulating me, Lady Hunstanton and Lady Caroline, and . . . every one. I hope I shall make a good secretary.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: You will be the pattern secretary, Gerald.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Talks to him .
You enjoy country life, Miss Worsley?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Very much indeed.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Don’t find yourself longing for a London dinner-party?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I dislike London dinner-parties.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: I adore them. The clever people never listen, and the stupid people never talk.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I think the stupid people talk a great deal.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Ah, I never listen!
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: My dear boy, if I didn’t like you I wouldn’t have made you the offer. It is because I like you so much that I want to have you with me.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Exit HESTER with GERALD.
Charming fellow, Gerald Arbuthnot!
He is very nice; very nice indeed. But I can’t stand the American young lady.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Why?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: She told me yesterday, and in quite a loud voice too, that she was only eighteen. It was most annoying.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: One should never trust a woman who tells one her real age. A woman who would tell one that, would tell one anything.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: She is a Puritan besides—
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Ah, that is inexcusable. I don’t mind plain women being Puritans. It is the only excuse they have for being plain. But she is decidedly pretty. I admire her immensely.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Looks steadfastly at MRS. ALLONBY.
What a thoroughly bad man you must be!
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: What do you call a bad man?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: The sort of man who admires innocence.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: And a bad woman?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Oh! the sort of woman a man never gets tired of.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: You are severe—on yourself.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Define us as a sex.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Sphinxes without secrets.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Does that include the Puritan women?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Do you know, I don’t believe in the existence of Puritan women? I don’t think there is a woman in the world who would not be a little flattered if one made love to her. It is that which makes women so irresistibly adorable.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You think there is no woman in the world who would object to being kissed?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY
